body:
Implement Phase 0 (only) of .adlc/specs/context-rot-threshold-calibration.md — §1.2 (Immediate Hotfix) and §1.3 (Recovery Exception), gated by AC0 in §4. This is the full self-contained scope; read the spec sections directly for exact grammar/wording, this ticket summarizes the required behavior and the verification commands.

Do NOT touch §2-§4 AC1-AC9 (Phase 1 host-protocol design) — it depends on host envelope capabilities (K_host, host_lock_fd, host_live_tokens/host_capacity_tokens, occupancy_bind_mac) that Claude Code and Codex do not expose today, and the spec's own §1.1 banner says implementing it now would recreate the exact outage this ticket fixes. Phase 1 is a separate future ticket.

BACKGROUND / ROOT CAUSE (spec §1): the context-rot handoff gate denies all mutating tool calls once a session crosses the handoff/hard band. In Claude Code and Codex it currently fires after ~2 tool calls in fresh sessions because (a) WARN_BYTES/HANDOFF_BYTES/HARD_BYTES are OR-joined into evaluateBands and get tripped by system-prompt/MCP-schema/rules overhead alone, before any real usage pressure exists, and (b) MAX_SCAN_BYTES was set equal to HARD_BYTES (256 KiB); exceeding it during the backward transcript scan set observed.depth = +Infinity, which evaluateBands treats as past every band — hard-locking any session whose on-disk baseline exceeds 256 KiB, which is the common case with several plugins/skills loaded, not a rare one. A prior incident from this bug denied every Bash call including the operator's own recovery CLI and even `pwd`, producing a total un-self-recoverable lockout.

WHAT TO BUILD:

1. Byte-threshold retirement (spec §1.2.1): Claude Code and Codex adapter call sites into evaluateBands MUST stop populating observed.bytes. evaluateBands already treats an absent signal as {warn:false, handoff:false, hard:false} for that signal (see bands.mjs's existing absent-signal handling) so no change to evaluateBands itself is required — only the two adapters' call sites change. Leave bytes support intact for any other, already-calibrated adapter (do not touch those call sites).

2. Retire MAX_SCAN_BYTES (spec §1.2.2): remove it as a distinct exported constant. The scan's only two budgets become MAX_ACTIVE_CONTEXT_BYTES (8 MiB) and MAX_SCAN_WALL_MS (a wall-clock budget; pick a value in the tens-of-ms-to-low-hundreds-of-ms range consistent with sequential reads of a few MB completing quickly on ordinary hardware — document the chosen constant). When the scan exceeds either budget before reaching start-of-file, report the tool-call count actually accumulated so far — never +Infinity, never treat an unbounded/malformed value as certainty. `Number.isFinite(observed.depth)` must hold whenever observed.depth isn't explicitly NaN for an unrelated fail-closed reason.
   - Phase 0 boundary policy: there is no K_host/MAC available in Phase 0, so no compaction-boundary-shaped record can ever be authenticated. Per the general 'unregistered compaction boundary' rule already in bands/scan logic (spec §2.1.2's rule, which already covers this — no new logic needed, just make sure Phase 0's scan actually follows it): the backward scan never stops early at a boundary-looking record; it always continues toward start-of-file (or the two budgets above), treating the entire on-disk transcript as one continuous epoch.
   - Lower-bound trust rule: a depth value accumulated before the budget was hit is a lower bound, not an exact answer. It is only safe to act on as an implicit "allow" once it already reaches HANDOFF_DEPTH (more unseen calls only make a deny/handoff more correct, never less). If the lower bound has NOT reached HANDOFF_DEPTH (including when it's in WARN range, e.g. 20-29), mutating tools other than the Recovery Exception and the Inspection Bash Exception (see #4/#5 below) remain restricted until a complete scan succeeds establishing a true, non-partial depth. This is narrower than Hard-Degraded Mode — it does not set depth to NaN, and a later evaluation that completes a full scan resolves normally.

3. Fresh/low-usage sessions must never trip any band on turn 0-2 (spec §1.2.3) — this is the regression the whole hotfix exists to close; it should fall out of #1 and #2 above, but must be tested end-to-end against the real hook entry points (adlc-hook.mjs / adlc-handoff-gate.mjs), not just bands.mjs/thresholds.mjs unit math, because the original incident was a hook-payload-to-decision integration failure.

4. Recovery Exception (spec §1.3): before any other Hard-Degraded/deny check (band evaluation, scan-budget lower-bound restriction, or anything else that can deny a mutating tool), recognize and unconditionally ALLOW an invocation of the mutating tool that passes BOTH a tool-identity gate AND a command-line grammar match:
   - Tool-identity gate: Claude Code — input.tool_name is exactly 'Bash' or 'Shell' (reuse the existing check in plugins/adlc-claude-code/hooks/adlc-hook.mjs, don't re-derive it). Codex — read the tool name via toolNameOf(input) (reused from plugins/adlc-codex/hooks/adlc-handoff-gate.mjs) and test membership in this exception's own separate, narrow, exact allowlist: 'exec_command', the literal string 'functions.exec_command' (no other prefix before '.exec_command'), 'exec', 'Bash', 'bash', 'Shell', 'shell'. Do NOT reuse Codex's isShellToolName classifier for this allow-path (it's calibrated for the denial side, where over-inclusion is safe; here over-inclusion is dangerous) and explicitly exclude write_stdin/functions.write_stdin (delivers input to an existing process, not a standalone command) and run_command (excluded conservatively). A multi_tool_use.parallel envelope or any composite/nested tool call is a non-match at the top level even if it contains an eligible name as a child.
   - Command grammar: match against the single shell command string (not argv). First check the raw string for any CR/LF byte anywhere in it BEFORE tokenizing — a match on that is an immediate non-match for the whole string. Tokenize on a single ASCII space only (not other whitespace), except inside a properly single-quoted PATH_GRAMMAR span. Extraction of the command string is host-specific: Claude Code uses tool_input.command directly; Codex uses collectCommandText (reused from adlc-handoff-gate.mjs, NOT isShellToolName) and requires exactly one non-empty candidate — zero or more than one candidates is a non-match.
     - PATH_GRAMMAR = `[A-Za-z0-9_./=-]+` OR a single-quoted form whose content is any byte except a literal single-quote/NUL/newline (POSIX literal semantics, no escapes). Applies only to token 1 (interpreter) and token 2 (script) — both always adapter-controlled, never attacker-chosen.
     - VALUE_GRAMMAR = `[A-Za-z0-9_./=:-]+` (unquoted only). Applies to the subcommand token and every flag/value token (3rd token onward). The colon is included specifically so `unlock --started-at <ISO-8601 timestamp>` can match byte-for-byte.
     - Token 1 must match PATH_GRAMMAR, be absolute (starts with '/') once unquoted, and its fs.realpathSync-resolved value must equal the adapter's own realpath-resolved process.execPath.
     - Token 2 must match PATH_GRAMMAR, be absolute once unquoted, resolved via fs.realpathSync freshly at match time (not cached — closes a symlink-swap/TOCTOU window), and equal the package's own packages/context-handoff/bin/handoff.mjs (also realpath-resolved).
     - Token 3 must match VALUE_GRAMMAR and be exactly one of: bypass, unlock, repair, write, resume.
     - Token 4 onward alternates flag-name / flag-value: a flag-name token starts with exactly '--' and must be one of that subcommand's own whitelisted flags (see per-subcommand list below); '--flag=value' single-token form is NOT supported (falls through to ordinary evaluation). Boolean flags (--write, --json) take no value token; every other whitelisted flag takes exactly one following VALUE_GRAMMAR value token.
     - Per-subcommand whitelisted flags (from the real CLI, packages/context-handoff/bin/handoff.mjs): bypass: --session --ticket --write --json (NOT --unbound-reason, which is free text and falls through). unlock: --session --pid --started-at --host --nonce --write --json. repair: --session --ticket --content-hash --host --write --json. write: --session --ticket --host --content-hash --write --json. resume: --session --deny-session --write --json.
     - Same-session binding: every --session flag-value (present in all five subcommands) MUST equal resolveHandoffSessionId (packages/context-handoff/lib/adapter.mjs's existing session-id resolver; the spec prose calls it resolveSessionId — same function) exactly — a grammatically valid but different session id is a non-match. --deny-session (resume only) is exempt from this binding (its whole purpose is naming a different, prior session) but still must satisfy VALUE_GRAMMAR.
     - A duplicate flag name, an unknown flag for that subcommand, a value-taking flag missing its value (or followed immediately by another flag name), or a boolean flag followed by a stray value token is a non-match.
   - Best-effort audit logging: every allowed recovery-CLI invocation attempts to record to the manifest evidence trail (existing recordOrExit/gate mechanism) tagged 'context-handoff-recovery-under-band'. The permissionDecision:'allow' is NEVER gated on this record succeeding — record after deciding allow; a logging failure surfaces as a diagnostic warning only, never flips allow to deny.
   - No-safe-session-id branch: when resolveHandoffSessionId (packages/context-handoff/lib/adapter.mjs's existing session-id resolver; the spec prose calls it resolveSessionId — same function) yields nothing (no candidate at all), no --session-bearing recovery command can be built. In this case ONLY, the deny/degraded diagnostic message must state plainly (a) that no session id could be resolved, (b) instruct the operator to end the session and start a new one, and (c) state that `pwd` remains usable in the interim — and must NEVER print a --session/--deny-session-bearing command in this branch.

5. Inspection Bash Exception (spec §1.3): an invocation whose command line is the exact literal `pwd` (no arguments, no shell metacharacters, no chaining) is allowed unconditionally regardless of band state or scan/depth completeness, on both hosts, evaluated by the same tool-identity-gate + matcher mechanism as #4 (not a separate code path). This exists so the incomplete-scan lower-bound restriction (#2) can never re-create the original 'even pwd was denied' outage.

6. Diagnostic messages: every Hard-Degraded/deny permissionDecision response, when a safe session id IS resolvable, MUST include the literal, copy-pasteable recovery command with BOTH the interpreter and script given as the adapter's own realpath-resolved absolute paths (never a bare `node` or a repo-relative script path). Either path token must be single-quoted whenever it contains any character outside `[A-Za-z0-9_./=-]` (e.g. a worktree path containing a space).

ACCEPTANCE CRITERIA (verbatim from spec §4 AC0, all already spec-lint-verified — run `adlc spec-lint .adlc/specs/context-rot-threshold-calibration.md` to confirm no regression):

1. Fresh-session regression: a brand-new session (0-2 prior tool calls) on Claude Code or Codex, any model including unrecognized ones, → `pwd` (or equivalent minimal Bash/execute_command) is ALLOWED. Verify: fresh-session fixture in handoff-deny.test.mjs asserts permissionDecision === 'allow' for both hosts, running against the real hook entry points end-to-end.
2. Large-baseline fresh-session regression: same as above but with a baseline blob sized 256 KiB-8 MiB (large enough to have tripped the old MAX_SCAN_BYTES, well within the new MAX_ACTIVE_CONTEXT_BYTES) → the scan completes within MAX_SCAN_WALL_MS, establishes exact depth 0-2, and ordinary mutators (Edit, Write, a normal non-pwd Bash call) are ALLOWED, not merely pwd. Must use a real >256 KiB fixture — a small-transcript fixture cannot detect this regression.
3. Compaction-boundary decoy: a transcript with a well-formed compaction-boundary-shaped record partway through (0-2 real tool calls after it, substantially more before it) — under Phase 0 the scan must NOT stop at it and must NOT report the low post-boundary count; it continues to start-of-file/budgets and reports the true cumulative count. Verify: assert reported depth equals the full pre-boundary count, not the post-boundary count.
4. Cumulative post-compaction transcript >8 MiB: small current active content but >8 MiB cumulative on-disk history hits the same incomplete-scan lower-bound restriction (disclosed, not a bug) — verify pwd and the Recovery Exception still allow while an ordinary Bash/Edit call is restricted.
5. Byte-threshold retirement: a transcript of any size with a completely-scanned, proven low depth (< WARN_DEPTH) → allow, even when the file exceeds the old 256 KiB HARD_BYTES value. Verify: assert observed.bytes is absent from both adapters' call sites into evaluateBands.
6. No +Infinity, no MAX_SCAN_BYTES: a scan exceeding MAX_ACTIVE_CONTEXT_BYTES/MAX_SCAN_WALL_MS before reaching start-of-file reports the actually-accumulated count, never +Infinity. Verify: assert Number.isFinite(observed.depth) and that MAX_SCAN_BYTES no longer exists as an exported constant. Must test against a real oversized (>256 KiB, <8 MiB) fresh-session fixture, not only small transcripts.
7. Recovery Exception matcher-level tests (the full grammar spec above): positive fixtures for every one of the five subcommands' complete flag sets including a session id as a flag value; a real unlock --started-at reproducing an actual lock's ISO 8601 timestamp; a quoted PATH_GRAMMAR token containing $, &, (, ; as literal path bytes; decoys rejected for wrong path, shell metacharacters, chained commands, unlisted subcommand, unrecognized flags, non-absolute interpreter/script, symlink/TOCTOU-replaced path identity mismatch; a raw newline inserted at a token boundary rejected outright (proves CR/LF checked before tokenization); a namespaced/spoofed tool_name (e.g. mcp__something__Bash) rejected by the identity gate before grammar evaluation even with an otherwise-exact match; a --session value naming a different (but grammatically valid) session rejected, paired with a positive fixture proving resume --deny-session <other-session> is still accepted; for Codex specifically — positive fixtures for exec_command / functions.exec_command / exec under both tool_name and recipient_name, with command text under both command and cmd (including the combination recipient_name:'functions.exec_command', tool_input.cmd:'pwd'); negative fixtures for write_stdin/functions.write_stdin with chars:'pwd', for run_command, for evil.exec_command (attacker prefix before the dot), and for a multi_tool_use.parallel envelope carrying an eligible nested child call. Also assert the diagnostic message string itself: both interpreter and script as resolved absolute paths, matched from a nested/non-root working directory (cwd-independence), and from a worktree path containing a space (quoting works end-to-end).
8. Denial message contains the recovery command: every Hard-Degraded/deny diagnostic, when a safe session id was resolvable, includes the literal session-specific recovery command. When no safe session id was resolvable, the diagnostic instead contains all three required elements (no id resolved / start a new session / pwd remains usable) and asserts no --session/--deny-session-bearing command appears anywhere in that response. A subprocess fixture per adapter drives this branch via an envelope with no session_id/sessionId and an unsafe transcript_path basename.
9. Verification suite: subprocess tests in plugins/adlc-claude-code/hooks/test/handoff-deny.test.mjs and plugins/adlc-codex/hooks/test/handoff-deny.test.mjs, plus a new fresh-session end-to-end fixture exercising the real hook entry point (not a unit-level call into bands.mjs alone).

Run `node --test packages/context-handoff/test/ plugins/adlc-claude-code/hooks/test/ plugins/adlc-codex/hooks/test/` (or the repo's `npm test`/`run-tests.mjs` equivalent) to verify the full suite stays green, and `adlc spec-lint .adlc/specs/context-rot-threshold-calibration.md` to confirm AC0 stays fully verified (Phase 1's AC1-AC9 wishes are expected and out of scope).

NOTE ON EXISTING REGRESSION TEST THAT MUST CHANGE: packages/context-handoff/adapter-test/no-adapter-threshold-literals.test.mjs's 'the read window is taken from the package' test currently asserts the Codex hook's source contains the literal `maxScanBytes: api.HARD_BYTES` (the exact MAX_SCAN_BYTES==HARD_BYTES equation that spec §1.2.2 identifies as the root cause). Retiring that equation per this ticket means updating this pinned assertion to match the new maxScanBytes value/source (MAX_ACTIVE_CONTEXT_BYTES, not HARD_BYTES) rather than deleting the regression-test class itself; keep the surrounding 'no adapter-local threshold literal' enforcement intent (no re-declared MAX_SCAN_BYTES constant) intact, only its harcoded expected value changes. Do the equivalent check for the Claude Code hook's own local MAX_SCAN_BYTES constant and +Infinity depth trap (plugins/adlc-claude-code/hooks/adlc-hook.mjs, ~line 95 and ~lines 1580-1610's observeHandoffSignals) and its own pinned test coverage (cc-helper-drift.test.mjs, bands.test.mjs) for the same reason.

ADDENDUM (Round-5 adversarial review, scope expansion): the same false-lockout root cause this ticket exists to fix — an uncalibrated 256 KiB byte threshold tripping on a routine fresh-session baseline, independent of actual tool-call depth — was found to ALSO live in the separate `packages/build-gate` fitness-to-build gate (ticket T156), used by all three host plugins (Claude Code, Codex, Copilot) and running BEFORE the now-fixed handoff gate. A high-risk-ticket session with a >256 KiB transcript was still falsely locked out of an ordinary edit via build-gate, even after the handoff-gate fix above. Scope:

1. `plugins/adlc-claude-code/hooks/adlc-hook.mjs`'s `BUILD_GATE_BYTES_THRESHOLD` (buildgate mode): recalibrated from `256 * 1024` (aliasing HARD_BYTES) to `8 * 1024 * 1024` (matching context-handoff's own recalibrated `MAX_ACTIVE_CONTEXT_BYTES`).
2. `plugins/adlc-codex/hooks/adlc-build-gate.mjs`'s `DEFAULT_BYTES_THRESHOLD`: same recalibration.
3. `plugins/adlc-copilot/hooks/adlc-build-gate.mjs`'s `DEFAULT_BYTES_THRESHOLD`: same recalibration.
4. `packages/build-gate/lib/depth-signal.mjs` (the canonical source these three host copies are drift-tested against) is DELIBERATELY NOT recalibrated: its own test file, `packages/build-gate/test/depth-signal.test.mjs`, is a rail frozen by ticket T156 (not completed) and cannot be edited without a rails-bypass ceremony this ticket did not obtain. The three host hooks' own local constants are now a DISCLOSED, DELIBERATE divergence from the canonical package's default (documented in each file's own comment) — the comparison LOGIC (inclusive `>=`) has not drifted, only the DEFAULT VALUE, proven by each host's own drift test passing an explicit matching threshold instead of relying on both sides' defaults.
5. Each host's own `hooks/test/build-gate.test.mjs` (and Codex's `build-gate-recovery-exception.test.mjs` fixture, which used a 400 KiB pad to simulate "degraded" and needed bumping past the new 8 MiB threshold to keep its precondition true) updated accordingly — including a regression pin proving a routine ~400 KiB fresh-session transcript (well over the OLD threshold, comfortably under the new one) is no longer misclassified as degraded.

Verify: `node --test plugins/adlc-claude-code/hooks/test/ plugins/adlc-codex/hooks/test/ plugins/adlc-copilot/hooks/test/ packages/build-gate/test/` all green; `packages/build-gate/lib/depth-signal.mjs` and `packages/build-gate/test/depth-signal.test.mjs` show zero diff from main (rail respected).

ADDENDUM 2 (Round-5 adversarial review, deferred to a follow-up ticket): review also found that `countToolCalls` (the tool-call-count depth signal shared by the handoff gate and build-gate for Codex) does not recognize Codex's real, documented `role:"assistant"`/`tool_calls` transcript record shape (packages/context-handoff/serialization/codex-context-v1.md) — only Claude-style `"type":"tool_use"` records. This is the OPPOSITE failure direction from this ticket (under-counting/under-detection, not false-lockout over-triggering), pre-existing, and requires a real captured Codex transcript sample to fix correctly rather than a blind regex change against an unverified design doc. Deliberately NOT fixed here — tracked as T-01M05BWTEYKHEK3JJX71NXXJ4H.
title: Fix context-rot handoff false-positive lockout (Phase 0 hotfix + Recovery Exception)
